title: Implement signed performance manifests and shadow-pin orchestration for new model variants
creator: Marcus Patel
description: Goal: Define, implement, and operate an automated publishing pipeline that produces cryptographically-signed Redwood performance manifests for onboarded models and orchestrates a shadow-pin canary flow for variant pinning. The deliverable should include a stable manifest schema, signing & verification tooling, a staged publish/rollout pipeline, telemetry contract (latency/throughput/cost normalization), and a runbook for safe pin/rollback decisions.
acceptance_criteria: A schema v1.0 for performance manifests exists and is documented with examples (latency P50/P95, throughput, normalized cost per 1k tokens, hardware profile).

Automated manifest signing and signature verification is implemented in CI and runtime importer. Manifest artifacts are stored in the signed ledger (git-backed or artifact store) with immutable version tags.

Shadow-pin orchestration can route x% of traffic as shadow for a new variant, collect telemetry, and compute a pass/fail signal against pre-defined regression thresholds for latency, throughput, and cost.
A canary publish pipeline (staging -> regional mirror -> staged publish) exists and a single-button rollback mechanism is defined and tested on a synthetic workload.
Console surfaces the manifest version, signature verification status, and delta summary vs currently pinned variant (latency/cost tradeoffs) on the model catalog page.
Runbook and SLOs for rolling back a pin within the first 2 hours are documented and validated in a tabletop exercise.
tasks: Draft manifest schema (including normalization formula for cost across HW types).
Design signing strategy (key rotation, signing authority, signature format).
Build CI pipeline step to generate and sign manifests from benchmark bundle.
Runtime verification: implement manifest signature validation in onboarding flow and Console import path.
Shadow traffic harness: implement non-perturbing shadowing with sampling, KV cache warmup, and trace correlation.
Telemetry contract: define required metrics, tags, and dashboards for pass/fail calculation.
Integrate canary decision engine with rollout automation (percent steps and automatic rollback on failures).
UX: Console views for manifest diffs and pin controls (pin, unpin, force-rollback).
Security: coordinate with security team for KMS/HSM integration and key custody checks.

risks: If cost normalization formula is inaccurate across hardware types, manifest cost claims will mislead customers and cause billing disputes.
Signature key compromise would undermine trust; key custody and rotation are critical.
Shadow traffic may not surface long-tail regressions; need production-sampled backfills for high-variance workloads.
On-prem/private customers may require different signing and storage flows that complicate the publish pipeline.
notes: This ticket intentionally separates signing + ledger concerns from the visual UX implementation. Engineering leads should coordinate with infra/ops to ensure artifact immutability and with legal for wording on 'Redwood-verified' claims.
